pr_body: This commit fixes #64467. Note that Shader::has_param() in Godot 3.x still has the same issue.

issue_context.title: Shader.has_uniform() incorrectly reports uniforms as missing
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot 4.0 alpha14

### System information

Windows 10 64 bits GLES3 GeForce GTX 1060 6GB/PCIe/SSE2

### Issue description

I'm writing node configuration warnings that check shaders for specific uniforms required for some features to work in a node, but it seems no matter which uniform I test, `has_uniform` always return `false`. I need to be able to check them.

Workaround:
```gdscript
static func shader_has_uniform(shader: Shader, uniform_name: String) -> bool:
	var uniforms = RenderingServer.shader_get_shader_uniform_list(shader.get_rid())
	for uniform in uniforms:
		if uniform.name == uniform_name:
			return true
	return false
```

### Steps to reproduce

1) Have a shader with `vec3 uniform test_color;` which uses it, for example outputting to `ALBEDO`
2) Create a script which loads the shader and calls `shader.has_uniform("u_test_color")`
3) Observe it prints `false`, instead of `true`.


### Minimal reproduction project

[ShaderHasUniform.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9339392/ShaderHasUniform.zip)

review_comments:
Why do a linear search? (it's more expensive on a map than on a list also)
params_cache is a HashMap with the parameter name as key.

What is the point of the map if the difference is just that `shader_uniform/` is prepended?
There is a comment saying `//map a shader param to a material param..` but it's not very descriptive of what that really means. I guess "shader param" is the name of the parameter as seen in the shader? And values are the name of the parameter as saved in the material `.tres` file? In which case, prepending `shader_uniform/` in `has_uniform` isn't necessary as the map could be looked up by key.
Also if the prefix is added here, does that mean other places were missing it? (if not, they might come up with twice the  prefix, or break compat if they hadn't any)
